samples.text:
The diagram shows the steps for publishing a new book. There are eight steps and it start when the manuscript is sent and it finish when the books are in the shops.

Firstly, the author or their agent send the text of the book to a publisher. Then an editor looks at the manuscript and decide about it. If the manuscript is rejected, it is returned to the author and the process stops there. If it is accepted, a contract is signed and the fees and deadlines are agreed.

After that, the book is edited, the structure and the language are revised with the author. Next, the cover is designed and the pages are laid out, this is called design and typesetting. Then the book is proofread and the final errors are corrected.

When this is finished, the books are printed and bound. Finally, the books are sent to shops and online retailers for marketing and distribution.

Overall, publishing a book is a process with many different steps, and not every manuscript can be published because some of them are rejected in the assessment stage.
samples.why: Overview present though basic and repeated at the end · all stages including the rejection route covered · mechanical linking · adequate vocabulary · agreement errors and comma splices that do not block meaning.

samples.text:
The diagram outlines the process that a new book goes through, from the moment the manuscript is submitted until the finished books are distributed.

Overall, there are eight stages in the process. It is mostly linear, although at the assessment stage some manuscripts are rejected and sent back to the author, in which case they go no further.

At the beginning, the author or an agent submits the text to a publisher, where an editor assess it. Manuscripts that are rejected are returned, whereas those that are accepted move on to the contract stage, at which fees and deadlines are agreed. The text is then edited, with the author working together with the publisher to revise its structure and language.

Once editing is complete, the cover is designed and the pages are laid out in the design and typesetting stage. This is followed by proofreading, during which any final errors are corrected, so that the text is ready to be printed. The books are then printed and bound, and in the last stage they are marketed and distributed to both shops and online retailers.
samples.why: Clear overview noting the rejection point · stages logically sequenced with a good range of linkers · appropriate vocabulary (submits, laid out, bound) · mostly error-free with one agreement slip.

samples.text:
The diagram illustrates the eight stages through which a new book passes on its way from the author's desk to the retailer.

The process is essentially linear, beginning with the submission of a manuscript and concluding with the marketing and distribution of the printed books. Its one decision point comes early on, when an editor at the publisher either accepts the manuscript or returns it to the author.

To begin with, the text is submitted to a publisher either by the author or by an agent. It is then assessed by an editor, and any manuscript that is rejected is sent back, meaning the process ends there. For successful manuscripts, a contract is signed setting out fees and deadlines, after which the editing phase begins, with the structure and language being revised in collaboration with the author.

The book next moves into design and typesetting, where the cover is created and the pages are laid out. Proofreading follows, allowing any remaining errors to be corrected. Finally, the books are printed and bound before being marketed and dispatched to bookshops and online retailers.
samples.why: Well-placed overview identifying the single decision point · every stage covered with fluent sequencing · precise vocabulary (in collaboration with, dispatched) · wide range of passive and participle structures · error-free.
